- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 5-day avg); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Model overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 → -0.5 → +0.5), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- When true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.  
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often misses sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1% per day to forecast for next 7–10 days.
